exec: // A product ID that does not exist must return 404 (Not Found)
pm.test('Status code is 404 for a non-existent product ID', function () {
pm.response.to.have.status(404);
// Verify the error response body is descriptive (not generic)
pm.test('Error response contains a descriptive message', function () {
var jsonData = pm.response.json();
pm.expect(jsonData).to.have.property('message');
pm.expect(jsonData.message).to.be.a('string');
pm.expect(jsonData.message.length).to.be.greaterThan(0);
console.log('Error message: ' + jsonData.message);

request.description: Step 2: GET /products/99999 — ID beyond range. Expect 404. Read the error message to verify it is descriptive.

item.name: 2.3 GET Product with Zero ID - Boundary Test

exec: // Boundary test: ID=0 is below the minimum valid ID (1) and should be rejected
pm.test('Zero ID is treated as invalid (expect 404)', function () {
pm.response.to.have.status(404);
// Document the actual API behaviour for this boundary case
pm.test('API returns a descriptive error for ID=0', function () {
var jsonData = pm.response.json();
pm.expect(jsonData).to.have.property('message');
console.log('[Boundary] GET /products/0 — Status: ' + pm.response.code + ' | Message: ' + jsonData.message);

request.description: Step 3: GET /products/0 — boundary test. Is 0 a valid ID? Document the status code and message.
